title: Rav Dimi, Brother of Rav Safra
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Nedarim 77b: “Rav Dimi, the brother of Rav Safra, recited this baraita: Whoever vows, even though he fulfills it, is called a sinner.” In Arakhin 16a, when Rav Dimi fell ill, Rav Safra his brother went to visit him. Dimi said: “May it come upon me that I have fulfilled everything the Rabbis said.” Safra asked Dimi: “Did you fulfill this: A person should never recount the good of his fellow, for from his good he comes to his disgrace?” Dimi replied: “I had not heard it; had I heard it, I would have fulfilled it.” In Ketubot 85b his death is mentioned, for they said there: a certain man deposited a silk garment with Rav Dimi, the brother of Rav Safra; he died without instructions. The depositor came before Rabbi Abba, who said to him: “I know of Rav Dimi that he was not wealthy.”

notes.text: Saved Davidson Arakhin16a has Dimi ill and Safra visiting, then Safra’s question and Dimi’s answer. Its plural אמר להו is represented without inventing an extra named participant. The old reversed-speaker note is withdrawn in the current edition; prior versions remain. The Ketubot depositor, not deceased Dimi, approaches Rabbi Abba.

The consulted Arakhin 16a explicitly has Dimi ill and Safra visiting, followed by Safra’s question and Dimi’s reply. The plural “he said to them” is retained in the source record without inventing another named visitor. The old reversed-role note remains historical; the current note is preserved verbatim. The Ketubot depositor is distinct from the deceased depositary.
